#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Phase 6 runtime demonstration of the local stack (US-009 change run). Prints statuses, counts and
# registration data created here only; never credentials or .env values.
set -u
cd "$1"   # 02_output
ENVF=../.env
export COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=konferenca-us009
DC="docker compose --env-file $ENVF"
U="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' $ENVF | tr -d '\r')"
P="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' $ENVF | tr -d '\r')"
AUTH=(-u "$U:$P")
B=http://127.0.0.1:8080
F=http://127.0.0.1:8081
STAMP=$(date +%s)
code() { curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$@"; }
wait_ready() { for i in $(seq 120); do [ "$(code $B/actuator/health/readiness)" = 200 ] && return; sleep 2; done; echo "backend not ready"; }

echo "== start: $DC up -d --build (project $COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME)"
$DC up -d --build >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "exit $?"; wait_ready
$DC ps --format '{{.Service}}: {{.Status}}'

echo "== NFR-04 health"
for p in /actuator/health /actuator/health/liveness /actuator/health/readiness /actuator/env; do echo "$p -> $(code $B$p) $(curl -s $B$p | head -c 40)"; done

echo "== DoD-P01 registrations through the frontend proxy"
EXT=$(curl -s -X POST $F/api/registrations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"type\":\"EXTERNAL\",\"firstName\":\"Demo\",\"lastName\":\"Zunanja$STAMP\",\"email\":\"demo.ext.$STAMP@example.org\",\"organization\":\"Demo d.o.o.\",\"options\":[\"ws-ai\"],\"consents\":[\"privacy\"],\"captchaToken\":\"test-pass\"}")
STU=$(curl -s -X POST $F/api/registrations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"type\":\"STUDENT\",\"firstName\":\"Študent\",\"lastName\":\"Čebelar$STAMP\",\"email\":\"demo.stu.$STAMP@example.org\",\"studyInstitution\":\"Univerza\",\"studyProgramme\":\"Računalništvo\",\"studentId\":\"S$STAMP\",\"options\":[],\"consents\":[\"privacy\"],\"captchaToken\":\"test-pass\"}")
echo "external: $EXT"; echo "student: $STU"
EID=$(echo "$EXT" | sed -n 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p'); SID=$(echo "$STU" | sed -n 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
echo "rejected captcha: $(code -X POST $F/api/registrations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"type":"EXTERNAL","firstName":"X","lastName":"Y","email":"x@example.org","organization":"O","options":[],"consents":["privacy"],"captchaToken":"wrong"}')"

echo "== DoD-P02 database rows and JSON copies"
$DC exec -T postgres psql -U registration -d registration -At -c "select type, last_name from registration where id in ('$EID','$SID') order by type"
$DC exec -T backend ls /data/json-copies/$EID.json /data/json-copies/$SID.json
$DC exec -T backend cat /data/json-copies/$SID.json | grep -o '"studyProgramme":"[^"]*"'

echo "== DoD-P03 Mailpit (subjects and attachment counts only)"
sleep 2
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8025/api/v1/search?query='"$STAMP"'&limit=50' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d["messages"]), "messages mentioning the run stamp"); [print(" ", m["Subject"], "attachments", m["Attachments"]) for m in d["messages"]]'

echo "== DoD-P04 export"
echo "with credentials: $(code "${AUTH[@]}" $B/api/export -o /tmp/claude-1000/demo-export.xlsx) $(file -b /tmp/claude-1000/demo-export.xlsx 2>/dev/null | head -c 40)"
echo "without credentials: $(code $B/api/export)"; echo "wrong password: $(code -u "$U:wrong-$STAMP" $B/api/export)"

echo "== DoD-P06 search (API) and organizer page"
S=$(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations?text=%C4%8Debelar$STAMP")
echo "by last name: $(echo "$S" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("total", d["total"], [ (i["lastName"], i["type"]) for i in d["items"]])')"
T=$(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations?type=STUDENT&text=$STAMP")
echo "by type STUDENT + stamp: $(echo "$T" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("total", d["total"], [ (i["lastName"], i["type"]) for i in d["items"]])')"
T=$(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations?type=EXTERNAL&text=$STAMP")
echo "by type EXTERNAL + stamp: $(echo "$T" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("total", d["total"], [ (i["lastName"], i["type"]) for i in d["items"]])')"
echo "through the frontend proxy: $(code "${AUTH[@]}" "$F/api/registrations?text=$STAMP")"
echo "without credentials: $(code "$B/api/registrations?text=$STAMP") body bytes $(curl -s "$B/api/registrations?text=$STAMP" | wc -c)"
echo "wrong password: $(code -u "$U:wrong-$STAMP" "$B/api/registrations")"
echo "wrong password with X-Requested-With: $(code -u "$U:wrong-$STAMP" -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' "$B/api/registrations"), WWW-Authenticate: $(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -u "$U:wrong-$STAMP" -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' "$B/api/registrations" | grep -ci www-authenticate)"
echo "invalid parameters: $(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations?type=VISITOR&page=0")"
echo "organizer page /organizer: $(code $F/organizer) $(curl -s $F/organizer | grep -o '<div id="root">' )"

echo "== security headers"
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations" | grep -iE '^(content-security-policy|x-frame-options|x-content-type-options|referrer-policy|cache-control):' | tr -d '\r'
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null $F/organizer | grep -iE '^(content-security-policy|x-frame-options|x-content-type-options|referrer-policy):' | cut -c1-80 | tr -d '\r'
echo "client Host header via proxy: $(code -H 'Host: evil.example' $F/api/form-config)"
echo "20 KB body: $(head -c 20000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a' | curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST $F/api/registrations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @-)"
echo "SB-11 users: backend $($DC exec -T backend id -u), frontend $($DC exec -T frontend id -un)"

echo "== SR-03 rate limit on the search endpoint (62 requests in one minute)"
sleep $(( 61 - $(date +%S | sed 's/^0//') ))
R=$(for i in $(seq 62); do code "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations?page=1"; echo; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "GET /api/registrations: $R"
echo "POST /api/registrations in the same minute (separate endpoint): $(code -X POST $B/api/registrations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}')"

echo "== NFR-02 down and up"
$DC down >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "down $?"; $DC up -d >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "up $?"; wait_ready
$DC exec -T postgres psql -U registration -d registration -At -c "select count(*) from registration where id in ('$EID','$SID')"
$DC exec -T backend ls /data/json-copies/$EID.json /data/json-copies/$SID.json
echo "search after recreation: $(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "$B/api/registrations?text=$STAMP" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("total", json.load(sys.stdin)["total"])')"
$DC ps --format '{{.Service}}: {{.Status}}'

echo "== backend log: personal data of this run"
echo "lines with the run's names or emails: $($DC logs backend 2>&1 | grep -cE "Zunanja$STAMP|Čebelar$STAMP|demo\.(ext|stu)\.$STAMP")"

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable programme, and give the required consent. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy; the participant gets a confirmation email and every organizer a notification with the JSON attached. Organizers download all registrations as an Excel workbook. Registrations are protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4.1 REST API under `/api` (Java 21): form configuration, registrations, export | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page built with Vite, served by nginx, which also forwards `/api/` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |
| local stack | `docker-compose.yml`: backend, frontend, PostgreSQL 16, Mailpit (mail catcher) | this file |

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, and a `.env` file at the repository root copied from `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` filled in.

```sh
cd 02_output
docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
```

| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://127.0.0.1:8081 | registration page |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config | API (backend directly) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export | Excel export (HTTP Basic with `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness | readiness |
| http://127.0.0.1:8025 | Mailpit: every email sent by the stack |

Locally the reCAPTCHA runs in test mode (a "test mode" checkbox on the page). The settings `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` (default `true` locally), `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default `60`) and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` (default `false` locally, D-11) can be overridden when starting, for example `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; registrations and JSON copies stay on the named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes them).

The end-to-end tests run against this stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#end-to-end-tests).

On Windows, clone into a short path or with `git clone -c core.longpaths=true …`: some Java test paths exceed 260 characters below a deep folder.

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, behaviour, settings, deployment, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, database schema, JSON copy and configuration schemas, emails, reCAPTCHA, UI |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition of done, security evidence, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision of the run |
| [docs/01_requirements-check.md](docs/01_requirements-check.md), [docs/00_preflight-report.md](docs/00_preflight-report.md) | requirements check, environment check |
# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Agent: writes

Version 1.0.0 of the conference registration (backend and frontend), 2026-10-21.

## Delivered

- Registration forms for external participants (US-001) and students (US-002) with exactly the fixed fields of each type, the options available to the type grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the mandatory `privacy` consent, never preselected.
- Conference options and consents from a configuration file (`CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH`, schema in `docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`); an invalid file stops the backend at start (US-003).
- Confirmation in the page only after the backend accepted the registration; field errors next to their fields; a general message without technical details on failures (US-004).
- Storage in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy per registration, both before the success answer (US-005, AR-05).
- Participant confirmation email and one organizer notification per configured address with the JSON copy attached; a mail failure never undoes a registration (US-006, US-007).
- Excel export for the organizer over HTTP Basic, refused over plain HTTP from non-local clients (US-008, SR-06).
- reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the backend, a deterministic test mode for local and test use, rate and body-size limits, security headers, non-root containers, health and readiness endpoints.
- Local stack with `docker compose` (backend, frontend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit); data on named volumes survives container recreation.

Verification: 35/35 acceptance criteria tested; 311 automated tests green (backend 251, frontend 55, end-to-end 5); line coverage backend 99.11 %, frontend 100 %; mutation score backend 99.10 % adjusted (96.70 % raw), frontend 90.85 %; no open Critical or High finding (`docs/06_verification-report.md`).

## Known limitations

- Medium, accepted (`docs/06_verification-report.md`): the pinned Vite 6.4.3 has advisory GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv in its dev server (not in the shipped bundle; fix 6.4.4 needs approval, D-16); `qs` advisories only through Stryker (PA-03); nginx `/api/` location without `internal`; no npm `min-release-age` (needs npm 11.10).
- The rate limit is kept in memory per backend instance and counts per client address and endpoint; behind several backend instances the limit applies per instance.
- Email addresses are accepted with an ASCII domain only (D-09); text fields are limited to 200 characters, email to 254 (D-08).
- The local stack runs with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` (D-11); production refuses that setting.
- Registrations and JSON copies are never deleted automatically (OQ-06): **the operator must delete the database rows and the JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference.**
- The end-to-end tests are not part of the mutation runs (D-15).
- Built and tested on the host with Oracle JDK 21.0.11 and Docker Compose 5.6.0 instead of the pinned Temurin 21.0.10+7 and Compose 5.5.1 (approved, D-02, D-03); the images use the pinned Temurin.

## Must be tested manually by a human

From `project/00_setup/environments.md`, "External services":

1. **Google reCAPTCHA v2 with production keys:** set `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false`, `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`; the page shows the Google widget; one real registration succeeds; a registration without solving the widget is refused.
2. **SMTP delivery to a real mailbox:** with the production SMTP settings (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS=true`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`), the participant confirmation and the organizer notification with the JSON attachment arrive in real mailboxes and are not marked as spam.
3. **TLS and the reverse proxy:** the external nginx with Let's Encrypt serves `/` from the frontend over HTTPS, redirects HTTP to HTTPS, forwards `/api` to the backend, sets the upstream `Host` itself (SR-08) and sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`; the organizer export works over HTTPS and is refused (403) over plain HTTP.
4. **Production start guard:** start the backend with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` and the production settings; it starts, and it refuses to start when `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` (SR-02).

## Decisions pending review

| Decision | Applied default |
|---|---|
| D-08 | text fields at most 200 characters, email at most 254 |
| D-09 | email: atext local part, ASCII domain with at least one dot |
| D-10 | rate limit default 60 requests per minute per client and endpoint |
| D-11 | local compose stack with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` |
| D-16 | Vite 6.4.3 kept; approve 6.4.4 in `tech-stack.md` for the next run |

All other decisions (D-01 … D-17) are resolved; see `docs/decisions-log.md`.

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API of the conference registration (`docs/02_contracts/openapi.yaml`), root package `si.konferenca.registration`, ports-and-adapters layout (`docs/02_specification.md` section 2).

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (pinned: Eclipse Temurin 21.0.10+7; this run built with Oracle JDK 21.0.11, D-02). Maven comes with the wrapper (`./mvnw`, Maven 3.9.9).
- Docker for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL 16.15 and Mailpit 1.31.1).
- For `run`: a PostgreSQL database and an SMTP server, for example the local stack's (`docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d postgres mailpit` in `02_output/`; publish their ports or use the full stack instead).

## Configuration

All settings are environment variables (`docs/02_specification.md` section 4). Secrets come from `.env` (keys listed in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example`) and have no default.

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `local` | `production` refuses unsafe settings at start (SR-02) |
| `DB_URL`, `DB_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration`, none (secret) | |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false`, empty, empty | SMTP account only in production (secret) |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.local` | |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none (secrets) | comma-separated recipients; export login |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` | `classpath:conference.json` | options and consents, schema `docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`; an invalid file stops the start |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `./data/json-copies` | persistent storage in production |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | `true` only locally and in tests: token `test-pass` |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty (secrets) | required in production |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | must stay `true` outside local plain HTTP (SR-06) |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | CORS for the Vite dev server only |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | `60`, `16384` | SR-03 |

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| build | `./mvnw -DskipTests package` (jar in `target/`) |
| test | `./mvnw verify` (unit, architecture and acceptance tests; JaCoCo report in `target/site/jacoco/`) |
| check | `./mvnw compile spotless:check pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check` (format with `./mvnw spotless:apply`) |
| run | `./mvnw spring-boot:run` with the settings above, for example `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=… ORGANIZER_USERNAME=… ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=… ORGANIZER_EMAILS=… CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true ./mvnw spring-boot:run` |
| mutation | `./mvnw org.pitest:pitest-maven:1.30.0:mutationCoverage -Dthreads=4` (about 25 minutes; report in `target/pit-reports/`) |
| dependency scan | `NVD_API_KEY=… ./mvnw org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0:check` (online; suppressions in `dependency-check-suppressions.xml`) |
| container | `docker build -t registration-backend .` (multi-stage, runs as uid 10001) |

## Troubleshooting

- `Could not resolve placeholder 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD'` (or an organizer setting): the secret is not set in the environment.
- `Invalid conference configuration: …` at start: the options file does not match its schema; the message names the entry.
- `Refusing to start in production: …`: a setting listed in the message is unsafe for `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`.
- Tests fail with Docker errors: start Docker; Testcontainers needs it.
- `GET /api/export` answers 403 with valid credentials: `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` and the request is plain HTTP from a non-local address; use HTTPS through the proxy.
- 429 responses: more than `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` requests per minute from one client to one endpoint.
# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React 19 single page for the registration form (`docs/02_contracts/interfaces.md`, "Registration form"), built with Vite and served by nginx. It talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01) and holds no secret: the reCAPTCHA site key comes from `GET /api/form-config` (AR-07).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13.0 with npm 11.6.2 (`engine-strict` is on).
- For `run`: the backend on `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (the Vite dev server proxies `/api` there).

# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Agent: writes

Version 1.1.0 of the conference registration (backend and frontend), 2026-10-22: version 1.0.0 (base run `tanej_single-agent_sdd_v001_run-1`) plus the organizer registration search (US-009, change run `tjan_single-agent_sdd_v001_run-1-search`).

## New in 1.1.0

- Organizer search API `GET /api/registrations` (US-009, BR-09, BR-10): optional `text` (case-insensitive, any part of first name, last name, email, organization or study institution; at most 100 characters after trimming), `type` (`EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`), `option` (a configured option id) and `page`; all filters combined; newest first, 20 per page, with the total number of matches. Invalid parameters are answered 400 with an error per parameter; the same organizer access as the export (HTTP Basic, HTTPS or localhost only).
- Organizer search page at `/organizer`: sign-in, search field, type and option filters, result table and page navigation. The login stays in memory only; stored participant data is always shown as text (SR-09).
- The rate limit now counts per client, method and path, so organizer searches and participant registrations (`GET` and `POST /api/registrations`) have separate budgets.
- The Maven wrapper is executable from a clean checkout on Linux and macOS (D-23).

## Delivered (unchanged from 1.0.0)

- Registration forms for external participants (US-001) and students (US-002) with exactly the fixed fields of each type, the options available to the type grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the mandatory `privacy` consent, never preselected.
- Conference options and consents from a configuration file (`CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH`); an invalid file stops the backend at start (US-003).
- Confirmation in the page only after the backend accepted the registration; field errors next to their fields; a general message without technical details on failures (US-004).
- Storage in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy per registration, both before the success answer (US-005, AR-05).
- Participant confirmation email and organizer notifications with the JSON copy attached; a mail failure never undoes a registration (US-006, US-007).
- Excel export for the organizer over HTTP Basic, refused over plain HTTP from non-local clients (US-008, SR-06).
- reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the backend, a deterministic test mode for local and test use, rate and body-size limits, security headers, non-root containers, health and readiness endpoints; local stack with `docker compose`.

Verification (`docs/06_verification-report.md`): 48/48 acceptance criteria tested; 381 automated tests green (backend 281, frontend 94, end-to-end 6); the 116 frozen tests of 1.0.0 unchanged; line coverage backend 99.20 %, frontend 100 %; mutation score backend 99.18 % adjusted (96.99 % raw), frontend 91.19 %; no open Critical or High finding.

## Known limitations

- Medium, accepted: the pinned Vite 6.4.3 has dev-server advisories that `npm audit` rates High (launch-editor, `server.fs`); they are not in the shipped bundle and the human lowered them to Medium (D-22). `@vitest/mocker` ≤ 4.1.11 (test tooling, D-29) and `qs` through Stryker (PA-03) have Moderate advisories. **Approve Vite 6.4.5 and a fixed Vitest in `tech-stack.md` for the next run.** Also accepted: nginx `/api/` location without `internal`; no npm `min-release-age` (needs npm 11.10).
- The search folds upper and lower case of Č, Š, Ž in PostgreSQL with `lower()`; that needs a database with a UTF-8 locale (the pinned image has one). An option filter accepts every configured option id, also inactive ones (G-8); the page offers only the active options.
- Reloading the organizer page signs the organizer out (the login is kept in memory only, by design).
- The rate limit is kept in memory per backend instance; behind several instances it applies per instance.
- Email addresses are accepted with an ASCII domain only (D-09); text fields are limited to 200 characters, email to 254 (D-08).
- The local stack runs with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` (D-11); production refuses that setting.
- Registrations and JSON copies are never deleted automatically (OQ-06): **the operator must delete the database rows and the JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference.**
- The end-to-end tests are not part of the mutation runs (D-15).
- Host tools differed from the pins and were approved: base run Oracle JDK 21.0.11 and Compose 5.6.0 (D-02, D-03); this run Ubuntu OpenJDK 21.0.12.1, Docker Engine 29.3.1 and Compose 5.1.1 (D-19 … D-21). The images use the pinned versions.
- On the US-009 machine, volumes of an earlier stack were left in place; this run's stack used `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=konferenca-us009` (D-24). The old volumes `konferenca-registration_pgdata` and `_jsoncopies` (created 2026-10-06) can be deleted by the operator.

## Must be tested manually by a human

From `project/00_setup/environments.md`, "External services", plus the organizer search page:

1. **Google reCAPTCHA v2 with production keys:** set `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false`, `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`; the page shows the Google widget; one real registration succeeds; a registration without solving the widget is refused.
2. **SMTP delivery to a real mailbox:** with the production SMTP settings, the participant confirmation and the organizer notification with the JSON attachment arrive in real mailboxes and are not marked as spam.
3. **TLS and the reverse proxy:** the external nginx with Let's Encrypt serves `/` and `/organizer` from the frontend over HTTPS, redirects HTTP to HTTPS, forwards `/api` to the backend, sets the upstream `Host` itself (SR-08) and sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`; the organizer export and search work over HTTPS and are refused (403) over plain HTTP.
4. **Production start guard:** start the backend with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`; it starts with the production settings and refuses to start when `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` (SR-02).
5. **Organizer search page in the organizers' browsers** (US-009): sign in with a wrong password (an error, no browser login dialog, no data), then with the right one; search a known participant by part of the last name in another case, filter by type and by option, page through more than 20 registrations; reload the page and check that it asks for the login again.

## Decisions pending review

| Decision | Applied default |
|---|---|
| D-08 | text fields at most 200 characters, email at most 254 |
| D-09 | email: atext local part, ASCII domain with at least one dot |
| D-10 | rate limit default 60 requests per minute per client and endpoint |
| D-11 | local compose stack with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` |
| D-16 | Vite 6.4.3 kept (superseded by D-22: approve 6.4.5 for the next run) |
| D-26 | the 100-character search text limit counts the trimmed text |
| D-27 | strict search parameters: exact `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT`, configured option ids, page 1 … 999999 in digits; blank values rejected |
| D-29 | `@vitest/mocker` advisories accepted as Medium; vitest 4.1.11 kept |

All other decisions (D-01 … D-29) are resolved; see `docs/decisions-log.md`.
